notes.A: Clean and legible with a clear orange CTA on the Team card, but it is the most templated SaaS layout of the set.
notes.B: Tidy hero with a statement-to-ledger illustration, consistent green CTAs and a closing CTA band; solid but conventional, and the FAQ column sits oddly narrow.
notes.C: Condensed editorial type, ledger rules and hairline-divided plan columns look genuinely designed while prices and CTAs stay clear on desktop and mobile.
notes.D: Horizontal plan rows and warm paper texture feel distinct, but the hero price shows no currency sign and the stacked mobile table is less scannable for comparing.
notes.E: Best balance of trust and polish: serif and green palette, illustration that supports the brief, plans with CTAs, a clear comparison table with yes/no icons, and clean mobile.
notes.F: Plain and fast, with plans and the toggle in the first screen and consistent CTAs and a tidy table, but little personality.
notes.G: Distinctive serif with double-underlined prices and an editorial feel, but the mobile table breaks words mid-word and the plan CTAs are small and left-hung.
notes.H: Collage of old ledger photos and a giant wordmark push the plans well below the fold and the staggered plan blocks and tiny mobile text read as decoration over clarity.
notes.I: Plans, prices and CTAs all in the first screen as clean rows, with comparison table, answered FAQ and good mobile stacking; warm and credible, if close to D in look.
notes.J: Giant LEDGERLY PRICING headline is memorable but buries the plans, and the staggered multicolour cards and low-contrast toggle sacrifice scanning for style.
